paper_title: Oil-Price Exposure as a Single-Factor Smart-Beta Strategy
selected_experiment: Sections 5-7: optimizer-built positive, neutral and negative OILP long-short equity portfolios, with a factor-timing signal selecting which regime to hold (no empirical table is reported)
cannot_implement_reasons: Requires a commodity (oil) price series: the OILP signal is each stock's regression beta to monthly oil-price changes, and the timing signal is defined on oil returns
Requires non-equity control series (market, credit, consumer and employment proxies) in the exposure regression, i.e. data from several asset classes at once

economic_rationale.value: Oil-price innovations affect firms differently through production costs, revenues, demand conditions and discount rates; conditionally, higher oil returns favor positive oil exposure and lower oil returns favor negative exposure. No unconditional premium is claimed.

evidence.quote: Oil-price innovations can affect firms differently through production costs, revenues, demand conditions, and discount-rate

universe_and_filters.value: the available equity universe; no filters stated

evidence.quote: On each chosen construction date, solve a constrained optimization across the available equity universe.

value: monthly oil price level series (Factor Level, OilPrices.csv)
other risk control series: market, credit, consumer and employment proxies
historical residual returns from a trailing cross-sectional regression (optimizer objective)
factor-timing signal s(t) and threshold h
optimizer constraints: OILP targets, other factor targets, gross long/short allocations, name-level weight bounds

evidence.quote: separate equity returns and control series are required

signal_formula_words.value: Each security's OILP is its estimated coefficient on monthly simple oil-price changes in a regression of its returns on oil changes and other risk controls. An optimizer builds long-short portfolios with positive, zero or negative aggregate OILP; a timing signal s(t) chooses the positive regime when s(t) is at least h, the negative regime when s(t) is at most -h, and neutral otherwise.

evidence.quote: The coefficient b_i,oil is the security-level OILP exposure.

signal_formula_symbols.value: r_i(t) = a_i + b_i,oil r_oil(t) + G_i X(t) + e_i(t); r_oil(t) = P(t) / P(t-1) - 1; B_oil(w) = sum_i w_i b_i,oil; regime positive if s(t) >= h, negative if s(t) <= -h, neutral otherwise

evidence.quote: r_i(t) = a_i + b_i,oil r_oil(t) + G_i X(t) + e_i(t)
